holidays.name: National Spumoni Day
holidays.description: A salute to the three-flavored, fruit-and-nut-studded Italian ice cream. It's a good excuse to ask for a scoop with pistachio, cherry, and chocolate all in one bowl.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates spumoni, which came from Italian dessert traditions and became a staple of Italian-American restaurants.
holidays.funFact: The name comes from the Italian word 'spumone,' which relates to 'spuma,' meaning foam. That refers to the dessert's light, airy texture.

holidays.name: Take Your Cat to the Vet Day
holidays.description: A nudge for cat owners to book the checkup they've been putting off. Cats are famously good at hiding illness and even better at hiding from carriers.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial awareness observance of unclear origin. It encourages regular veterinary care for house cats, who often go to the vet less than dogs do.
holidays.funFact: Cats instinctively mask pain and illness, a survival trait inherited from wild ancestors. That makes routine exams one of the best ways to catch problems early.

holidays.name: National Senior Citizens Day
holidays.description: A day to thank, honor, and spend time with the older people in your life. Their stories, wisdom, and questionable-but-delicious recipes deserve a standing ovation.
holidays.origin: President Ronald Reagan proclaimed it on August 19, 1988, setting August 21 as a national day to recognize older Americans.
holidays.funFact: The proclamation was signed just two days before the date it designated. Since then, the day has been observed every August 21.
